we have identified IQGAP1 as a novel component of the CXR2 “chemosnapse”, which is a complex of proteins that interact with CXCR2 upon stimulation with chemokines.
IQGAP 1 is a novel CXCR 2-interacting protein and essential component of the “chemosynapses”.
IQGAP is an essential component of CXCR2 “Chemosynapses”.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the proteins that interact directly with CXCL8 and CXCR2 to initiate signaling pathways that lead to chemotaxis and other CXCR2-mediated cellular responses.
the identification and characterization of proteins that are essential components of the “chemosynapses” that are formed upon chemokine receptor activation.
identifying and characterizing the components of the “chemosynaptic” signaling complex that assemble upon chemokine receptor activation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the identification of novel CXCR2 binding proteins will provide insight into the complex signaling pathways that are initiated upon CXCR2 stimulation.
the CXCR2 chemosynapse is a complex of proteins that interact with each other upon chemokine stimulation to relay signals from CXCR2 to the cytoskeleton.
CXCR2 and IQGAP1 are essential for the chemotactic response and CXCR2 mediated cell migration in response to CXCL8.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IQGAP is an important component of the “chemosynapses” that transduce CXCR2 mediated cellular signaling processes.
IQGAP is essential for CXCR2 mediated neutrophil chemotaxis.
IQGAP 1 is a novel CXCR2 interacting protein and is essential for the proper assembly of the CXCR-2 “chemosnapse” which is required for chemotaxis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CXCR2 is part of a large signaling complex, and this complex is necessary for the transduction of chemokine receptor signals.

IQGAP-1 plays a role in the chemokine mediated signaling pathway.
